title: A two-coordinate projection cannot prove a space intersection

original_problem.statement: Classify the relation of l1(t)=(t,0,0) and l2(s)=(0,b*s,c), initially b=1, c=0.
original_problem.goal: Classify the two lines as intersecting, skew, parallel_distinct or coincident, and give the point if intersecting.

assumptions.description: Both direction vectors are nonzero, so each is genuinely a line.

methods.name: Two-coordinate projection then claim
methods.description: Solve only the x and y components for a candidate, then claim it is the space intersection.

correct_steps.explanation: Solve only the x and y component equations for a candidate (t, s).
Substitute the candidate into both full lines and claim the same space point.
Conclude the lines intersect at that point.

allowed_perturbations.description: Replace c with 1, offsetting the second line.
Replace b with 2, rescaling the second line's direction.

expected_failure_mechanisms: At c=1, the x/y projection still gives (t,s)=(0,0), but the z components 0 and 1 disagree; the lines are skew, not intersecting, because their directions are not parallel.

verification_rules.description: Substitute the claimed parameters into all three components of both lines.
Independently classify the relation from all three components and direction parallelism.

explanation_fragments.text: Solving only the x and y components finds a candidate, but it must also satisfy the z component. At c=1 it does not, and the directions are not parallel, so the lines are skew rather than intersecting.

review.basis: Independently approved by Claude Code, acting as implementer/reviewer under explicit user authorization after Codex hit a usage limit: hand-verified the z-residual mismatch at c=1, the cross product (0,0,b), the scalar triple product bc, and that b=2 is a pure re-parametrization leaving the relation and point unchanged.
